samples.summary: New exit-2 test does not cover the sibling silent-false path in the same function: a missing/empty head SHA
searchedFor: grep headRefOid in scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs (only fixture + the mid-gate move)
samples.evidence: The delta's stated principle is "unread evidence must not be reported as a red gate" and it converts `ciPassed`'s catch into `process.exit(2)`. But the first line of the same function, `if (!sha) return false;` (mark-ready.mjs:160), still reports "CI not green" when the PR read produced no `headRefOid` — and no test in mark-ready.test.mjs ever runs with `pr.headRefOid` absent/empty (the only occurrences are the fixture value `cafe7` and the `headAfter` mid-gate-move case). So the exact failure the new test claims to guard against (a silent draft forever, job SUCCEEDED) can still ship untested through the neighbouring branch of the function the diff edits.

samples.summary: The stderr assertion pins only the generic second line, so the diagnostic first line (workflow file + SHA + underlying error) is uncovered
samples.evidence: The test asserts only `assert.match(stderr, /tooling error, not a gate refusal/)`. The first line — `Failed to read runs of ${CI_WORKFLOW_FILE} for ${sha}: ${err.message}` — could be deleted or lose the file name, SHA and `err.message` entirely and this test would still pass, leaving an operator with a bare "tooling error" and nothing to diagnose. Other tests in this file (e.g. line 221 `/Failed to read PR #7/`, line 461 `/the head moved from cafe7 to beef8/`) do pin the informative part, so this one is narrower than its neighbours.

samples.summary: `!promoted(calls)` in the new test is near-vacuous: the process exits at gate 1, long before any mutation is reachable
samples.evidence: `ciPassed` is called at mark-ready.mjs:193, before gates 1b/2/3 and before any `ghMutate`. Any exit code other than a promotion path makes `pr ready` unreachable, so this assertion holds whatever the code under test does short of a wholesale reordering. Harmless as a belt-and-braces guard, but it is not additional coverage of the behaviour the test names.

samples.summary: The CI-read tooling error is only exercised with `--promote`, never in the dry-run path
searchedFor: read all tests in mark-ready.test.mjs; only line 552 runs without --promote
samples.evidence: `run(["7", "--promote"], okConfig({ fail: [...] }))` is the only invocation. `ciPassed` runs identically in a dry run (mark-ready.mjs:193 is above the `if (!promote)` branch), and a dry run that reported an unreadable CI workflow as exit 1 would mislead a human operator the same way. Low impact — the shared code path is the same — but the dry-run contract is otherwise tested (line 551) and this case is not.
